time.desc: The short video platform filed an emergency application with the Supreme Court, requesting a stay on the implementation of the "strip or ban" federal law until the final hearing.

The Supreme Court announced that it would fast-track the platform’s appeal against the “strike-or-ban” law and set an accelerated oral argument schedule, but did not immediately issue a temporary injunction.
The incoming national leader submitted a document to the Supreme Court requesting to postpone the legal divestiture cutoff to buy time to resolve the dispute through negotiations after taking office
The federal government files papers in the Supreme Court opposing the request to delay execution and urging the court to keep the law in effect as scheduled.
The Supreme Court held oral arguments on the "strike or ban" law, and the judges' questions focused on the trade-off between national security and free speech.

The current government has publicly stated that it will not immediately force the platform to shut down users on the legal effective date, and will transfer the subsequent enforcement pressure to the incoming new government.
The Supreme Court rejected the platform’s request for an emergency stay of execution and maintained the legal status of the “strip or ban” law taking effect as scheduled.
The Supreme Court made a final ruling upholding the ban, and the platform stopped serving locally and was removed from mainstream app stores.
Platform X Allied subsidiary files emergency motion in local federal court seeking judicial review of order closing local operations
Parent company appeals to court seeking extension of divestment or injunction cutoff until after incoming leader takes office

The Federal Court of Appeal once again rejected Platform X’s request for a stay of execution. The platform announced that it would appeal to the highest judicial authority and announced that it might shut down by the cutoff.
Several civil rights and free speech organizations jointly submitted an amicus brief to the highest judicial body urging to prevent the ban from taking effect.
The leader-elect made his first public endorsement of Platform X's continued operations at the rally, revealing the platform received billions of views during the campaign
The court held an oral argument on the platform ban case. Most judges expressed doubts about the platform’s claims and tended to support legislation based on national security.
The platform was briefly removed after the federal ban took effect, then restored service to users in the country as elected leaders promised a reprieve.
The elected leader's government enters talks with a technology company and outside investor group to take over the platform's global operations
Leaders publicly stated that they are negotiating with multiple parties to acquire the platform and said they would make a decision on the sale within dozens of days.
Leaders sign executive order extending ban by approximately two and a half months
Leaders sign executive order establishing government sovereign wealth fund and say it may use it to acquire the platform
The platform has been re-listed in the country's major app stores, but it will only be available to users who have downloaded it initially, and new users will not be able to download it yet.
Regulatory authorities sent letters to the two major app stores, promising not to pursue legal liability for hosting or distributing the platform during the extension period
The platform has been re-listed. If the government and the platform fail to reach an agreement on time, they may face delisting again.
The personal information protection agency of a neighboring country confirmed that a foreign AI chatbot company shared user data with the platform’s parent company and removed it from the platform.
